label: Pronouns
outcome: Lo studente sostituisce nomi e gruppi nominali con subject pronouns e object pronouns corretti, mantenendo il referente e scegliendo la forma in base alla funzione prima/dopo il verbo o una preposizione.
must_master: subject pronoun before the verb in normal statements
singular/plural reference with it vs they/them
simple replacement of repeated names while preserving reference

scope_boundary.possessives: Do not teach possessive adjectives or possessive pronouns; the possessives topic belongs to another content stream.
scope_boundary.reflexives: Do not teach myself/yourself/themselves or reflexive meaning.
scope_boundary.relatives: Do not teach relative pronouns who/which/that.
scope_boundary.indefinites: Do not teach someone/anyone/nobody etc. as part of this topic.
scope_boundary.advanced_reference: Keep reference chains short and explicit; no discourse-heavy anaphora beyond A1+/A2.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using an object pronoun as subject
using a subject pronoun after a verb
using a subject pronoun after a preposition

italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: Them are my friends. I see they often.
italian_learner_risks.target: They are my friends. I see them often.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using me instead of I in a compound subject

italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: I bought two books. I need it for school.
italian_learner_risks.target: I bought two books. I need them for school.

context_bank: objects such as phones, keys and tickets

requirements: teach position/function, not only memorised pairs
show pronouns after verbs and prepositions
increase autonomy from selection to production
no possessive forms as a learning target
approximately 60 percent standard and 40 percent challenge

quality_rejections: including possessive adjectives/pronouns as assessed content
turning the topic into a pronoun chart with repetitive substitution only
ambiguous gender/reference tasks with no clear antecedent
advanced reflexive, relative or indefinite pronouns
distractors that change the referent rather than test pronoun function unless clearly designed as reference tracking
titles that announce 'subject pronoun' or 'object pronoun' as the answer cue
difficulty created by long lexical content rather than reference tracking
